root_cause.text: The completion side switch in `rds_ib_send_unmap_op()` does not handle masked atomic opcodes (`IB_WR_MASKED_ATOMIC_FETCH_AND_ADD` and `IB_WR_MASKED_ATOMIC_CMP_AND_SWP`), so when these opcodes are used (as always done by `rds_ib_xmit_atomic()`), the function falls through to the default case, returns NULL for `rm` while leaving `send->s_op` set, leading to a NULL pointer dereference in `rds_ib_send_cqe_handler()` when accessing `rm->m_final_op`.
root_cause.evidence: The commit message explicitly states: "rds_ib_xmit_atomic() always programs a masked atomic opcode ... But the completion-side switch in rds_ib_send_unmap_op() only handles the non-masked opcodes, so a masked atomic completion falls through to default and returns rm == NULL while send->s_op is left set. rds_ib_send_cqe_handler() then dereferences the NULL rm via rm->m_final_op". The patch adds the two missing masked atomic opcodes to the switch case.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add missing handling for masked atomic work completions to ensure proper cleanup of atomic operations.
intent_record.what: Added two new case labels (IB_WR_MASKED_ATOMIC_FETCH_AND_ADD and IB_WR_MASKED_ATOMIC_CMP_AND_SWP) to the switch statement in rds_ib_send_unmap_op, duplicating the existing atomic handling code.
intent_record.how: Enables proper unmapping of atomic resources for masked atomic work completions, preventing resource leaks or incorrect behavior that occurred when these opcodes were unhandled.

grouping_result.intent: Add missing handling for masked atomic work completions to ensure proper cleanup of atomic operations.

candidates.rationale: This case handles non-masked atomic fetch-and-add completions but does not include masked variants. When a masked atomic opcode (IB_WR_MASKED_ATOMIC_FETCH_AND_ADD) is used, the switch falls through to the default case, causing a NULL pointer dereference when accessing rm->m_final_op.

This case handles non-masked atomic compare-and-swap completions but does not include masked variants. When a masked atomic opcode (IB_WR_MASKED_ATOMIC_CMP_AND_SWP) is used, the switch falls through to the default case, causing a NULL pointer dereference when accessing rm->m_final_op.

vuln_statements.explanation: This case handles only the non-masked atomic fetch-and-add completion. The absence of handling for IB_WR_MASKED_ATOMIC_FETCH_AND_ADD causes the switch to fall through to the default, leading to a NULL pointer dereference when rm is not set but send->s_op is left set.

This case handles only the non-masked atomic compare-and-swap completion. The absence of handling for IB_WR_MASKED_ATOMIC_CMP_AND_SWP causes the switch to fall through to the default, leading to a NULL pointer dereference when rm is not set but send->s_op is left set.
